summary.name: Terminator
summary.one_liner: Terminator is a terminal emulator that lets you run multiple GNOME terminals in one window and arrange them in flexible layouts.
use_cases: running several shell sessions side by side
managing many remote machines at once
working heavily at the command line
summary.what_it_does: Terminator puts multiple GNOME terminals inside a single window. Users can combine and recombine terminal panes to suit their preferred layout. The page describes it as originally a simple python script written by Chris Jones in 2007, and says it was inspired by quadkonsole and gnome-multi-term, and more recently by iTerm2 and Tilix. The page text does not list specific features beyond multi-terminal layout.
notable: Originally a roughly 300-line Python script by Chris Jones, started in 2007
Lets you combine and recombine multiple terminals in one window
Inspired by quadkonsole, gnome-multi-term, iTerm2 and Tilix
caveats: Page text does not state a license or pricing
Page text gives little detail on specific platforms beyond GNOME
